name: Munroe Island (Munrothuruthu)
tagline: Backwater craft walks — coir villages, canoe routes and small boatyards
summary: Cluster of eight islets in Ashtamudi Lake known for coir retting and weaving, narrow canals, hand‑paddled canoes and small backwater boatyards—ideal for craft walks and workshops.
description: Munroe Island (Munrothuruthu) is a group of small islets at the confluence of the Kallada River and Ashtamudi Lake in Kollam district. The island village lives on coconuts, fishing and small‑scale backwater crafts.

The place matters for craft and livelihood histories: you can see coir‑retting pits, women spinning coir yarn and traditional wooden canoes used for village transport. Small boatmen maintain and repair country boats in waterside yards and village lanes.

Visitors get intimate, low‑impact experiences — short canoe or kayak rides through narrow canals, guided craft walks to coir units, hands‑on demonstrations and simple homestay meals. It suits half‑day craft walks, sunrise canoe voyages and slow photography.
highlights: Traditional coir retting, spinning and weaving units at the water’s edge
Hand‑paddled wooden canoes and small shikaras — village boating circuits
Narrow mangrove ‘arches’ and canal routes ideal for kayaking and canoeing
Small, informal boat repair/maintenance yards and country‑craft scenes
Responsible‑tourism life‑experience packages and community craft visits
Easy day‑trip from Kollam with homestays and sunset shikara cruises

sections.heading: Background
body: Munroe Island (Munrothuruthu) is a cluster of eight tiny islets (about 13.4 km²) in the Ashtamudi backwaters, named after Colonel John Munro. The settlement relies on coconuts, inland fisheries and small‑scale crafts such as coir processing.

The island is a recognised backwater tourism spot in Kollam district; local and district tourism bodies run canal cruises and community life‑experience trails that include visits to craft units and fishing stops. The island has also attracted scientific attention because of local flooding and subsidence concerns, so travel remains sensitive to tides and weather.

sections.heading: Boatbuilding & coir craft
body: Coir work is visible across the island: husk‑soaking (retting) in brackish water, spinning of coir yarn and hand weaving or small unit work. These activities are primarily traditional village livelihoods and are best viewed respectfully from the canal or a village lane.

Boat‑related craft on Munroe Island centres on small wooden canoes and country boats. Local boatmen, repairers and small waterside yards keep these craft serviceable for daily life and tourist canal trips. Many visitor itineraries combine canoe/kayak rides with stops at coir units and simple demonstrations or short hands‑on sessions.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take an early‑morning canoe or kayak through the narrow canals and the mangrove arch to watch coir retting pits and village life at the water’s edge. Guided craft walks stop at coir units, simple workshops and homestays where you can watch and sometimes try spinning or weaving.

Book a responsible‑tourism life‑experience or a local guided village itinerary to include farming stops, a handicraft unit visit, local food and a sunset shikara cruise on Ashtamudi Lake. Small‑group kayaking and sunrise canoe voyages are widely offered and focus on quiet routes, birdlife and craft scenes.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Reach Munroe Island by road, rail or water. Nearest rail: Munroturuttu (Munroe Island) station; nearest major airport: Trivandrum International (about 80–85 km). Many visitors base in Kollam and take a half‑day or full‑day trip with a local canoe or shikara.

Book activities with a recognised local operator or the Keralam Responsible Tourism Mission Society trail to ensure community coordination and photography consent. Check tide and weather before you go; low‑lying parts flood at high tide and some village routes close in poor weather.

latest.text: Keralam Responsible Tourism 'Life Experience Trails' lists an active Munroe Island trail that includes a handicraft unit visit, canal cruise and community food stop (bookings accepted 5–60 days ahead).
Kerala Tourism destination page for Munroe Island highlights coir making, village cruises and district tourism canal trips as active offerings.

visitorInfo.bestTime: November to February (cool, dry; early mornings best for calm canal paddles)
visitorInfo.howToReach: From Kollam (25–30 km): road taxi to Munroturuttu station/jetty, or take a short train to Munroturuttu and connect by local boat or tuk‑tuk; Trivandrum airport ≈80–85 km.
etiquette: Ask permission before photographing people and craft units (KRTMS also requires consent for photography).
Wear sun protection and quick‑dry clothing; bring insect repellent for mangrove and canal walks.
Support local craft by buying small coir items from the village rather than from middlemen — ask guides where earnings go.
Confirm boat departures, life‑jacket availability and tide timings with your operator before travel.
